title: Burst profile validator and customer acceptance procedure
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Create a focused load-testing harness and acceptance procedure that validates Dedicated capacity against bursty and microburst traffic profiles customers commonly see. This ticket covers: (1) methodology for generating repeatable burst + sustain traffic mixes, (2) instrumentation and metrics to capture tail-latency, jitter, and token-level throughput under autoscaler transitions, (3) an automated validation runner for customer onboarding with pass/fail gates and artifact links, and (4) a documented acceptance checklist for Solutions/SEs to sign off before Dedicated handoff.
background: Customer onboarding runs have exposed gaps when customer traffic contains short, high-intensity bursts (e.g., chat apps, bursty API gateways). Existing ramp-and-sustain tests validate average throughput and long-tail stability but under-emphasize short-duration peak behavior that stresses queueing, batching alignment, and autoscaler ramping. This work complements the existing ramp/sustain and replay harnesses by focusing on burst fidelity and autoscaler interactions.
tasks: Design canonical burst profiles (single microburst, burst trains, poisson bursts, scheduled surges)
Implement generator module in the load harness that supports sub-second burst shapes and configurable tenant weightings
Add observability hooks: per-request token timing, KV cache hit/miss, queue depth, autoscaler decision events
Create pass/fail criteria and SLO thresholds for tail P95/P99/P999 latency and token throughput during burst windows
Wire up customer-runner: parameterized job spec + artifact bundle (charts, raw traces, summary) for SEs to run during onboarding
Document acceptance checklist and handoff playbook for Solutions/SEs
acceptance_criteria: Harness can reproduce at least three canonical burst profiles with deterministic seeds
Automated runner produces artifacts: time-series charts, percentile latency tables, and a machine-readable summary.json
Pass/fail gate defined: P99 latency during burst <= configured SLO (default 250ms) OR documented fallback plan triggered
Autoscaler transition events are correlated with latency spikes in generated artifacts
SE-run checklist validated in at least two customer onboarding rehearsals and signed off by Solutions lead
notes: Focus on making the harness deterministic and easy for SEs to run in customer's VPC (lightweight docker bundle). Avoid heavy invasive agents. The burst generator should be able to run against an endpoint URL with only an API key and tenant header.
comments: 2025-03-01 Aisha Khan: Kickoff - outlined problem statement and scoped the three canonical profiles we should support: single microburst (200-1000 QPS over 1-3s), burst train (multiple bursts spaced by 10-60s), and sustained surge (10x baseline for 2-5 minutes).

2025-03-03 Luca Marino: Implemented initial burst generator prototype in the harness. Tested single microburst against local cluster; observed queuing and a 2-3x P99 spike. Pushed branch to github (link in artifacts).
2025-03-05 QA: Replayed prototype against dedicated-staging; KV cache misses amplified tail for first burst — added metric capture for cache hit ratio and request-level cache tags.
2025-03-06 Eng Lead (Miguel Torres): Recommendation to correlate autoscaler logs (scale up/down events) with trace IDs. Added task to capture autoscaler decision timestamps from control plane events.

2025-03-08 Solutions (Priya Patel): Requested SE-friendly runner that outputs a single tarball with HTML summary + raw trace + machine summary. Drafted acceptance checklist items for customer signoff.

2025-03-11 Luca Marino: Added pass/fail summary generator. Default P99 threshold during burst set to 250ms; configurable per-customer. Ran two rehearsals with SEs — first run passed except for one tenant-weighting scenario; investigating batching alignment algorithm in runtime.
2025-03-12 Aisha Khan: Updated ticket with final tasks and set due_date to 2025-03-21. Plan to present the harness and checklist in Solutions weekly on 2025-03-18 for signoff.
